cards: Criteria and weights first. The owner agrees what matters and how much, before anyone sees a score. The reference has S = Σ (w × r): weight times rating, added up.
Evidence, then ratings. Each option is rated on each criterion from evidence — fault logs, ages, people served, cost — not from how loudly it's argued.
Sensitivity, honestly. Show how close the scores are and what would change the order. But changing the weights after seeing the scores is choosing the answer first.
The owner decides. The architect ranks; the CIO decides and records why. Each regional head argues for their rooms — that's their job.

W8.title: Break-glass accounts, service accounts and blast radius
W8.sum: How to pay down access debt without locking everyone out — and whose decision each step is.
cards: Break-glass, done right. Emergency accounts live in the vault under two-person control; every use is alarmed, logged and reviewed, and the password changes after each use. An envelope nobody can find is neither safe nor usable.
Service accounts are keys too. An account one system uses to log into another needs an owner, the least access that works, and a password that changes.
Blast radius. One key in sixty rooms means one change can reach all sixty. The reference has % = part ÷ whole × 100 for how much a key opens, and T = Σ stage times for how long a staged change takes.
Whose decision. Access, the vault and every account are security's; the change board approves the room changes; the architect maps the doors and stages the work. Governance only.

W9.title: Accessibility debt
W9.sum: How promised access quietly goes missing — and how a principal makes it a defect like any other.
cards: Requirements, not preferences. Captions everywhere and assistive listening in large rooms are in the standard. A room without them is failing the standard, not choosing an option.
Measure the gap. The reference has % = part ÷ whole × 100 for how far the estate falls short and P = n × a for what closing it costs. Gaps are recorded with owners and dates, like faults.

Silence isn't satisfaction. People who need access often adapt quietly — a phone app, a seat at the front — rather than be ‘the problem’. Don't wait for complaints. Never suppress an access alert as ‘expected’.

Tested by users. Accessibility checks go into every acceptance checklist, and the people who rely on captions and loops test them. Requirements are the accessibility lead's; installs each site's facilities'. Not legal advice.

W10.title: The principal's test
W10.sum: What it means for an architecture to respond without its architect — and how you'd know.
cards: Count what held without you. A threat is prevented by what was built, saved by someone trained, stepped into by you, or lost. Only the first two count. The reference has % = part ÷ whole × 100 for the share held without you.
Slow to reach is the design constraint. When every question to you costs minutes — T = Σ stage times for a round trip — the people and systems on the spot have to answer first.
Stepping in is allowed. It always works for today and always costs tomorrow: every save you make is a save the team didn't prove it could.
Leaving is a design step. Your access ends on your last day; every item with your name gets an owner; your number comes out of every runbook. Security owns access; the CIO owns the rest.

Q-A1.title: Check · Signal flow and gain staging

qs.q: The ceiling on a digital console's meter is…
qs.why: dBFS counts down from full scale. 0 dBFS is the highest value a digital system can represent.

qs.q: A vocal clips on every chorus. Where do you fix it first?
qs.why: Clipping happens at the preamp or converter. Lower the gain there, then use the fader to set the level.

qs.q: When should you set a singer's preamp gain?
o: At the loudest line they will really sing
qs.why: Gain has to leave headroom for the loudest real moment, not the quietest test.

qs.q: Which order is right?
For voltage or sound pressure, +6 dB is about…
For power, doubling is about…
A listener moves from 2 m to 4 m from a small source outdoors. The level changes by about…
qs.why: Doubling the distance in a free field spreads the sound over four times the area: about −6 dB.

qs.q: Why match levels before an A/B comparison?
o: Louder versions tend to be preferred, whatever changed
qs.why: Otherwise you are comparing loudness, not the change you made.

qs.q: The wavelength of a 343 Hz tone in air is about…
One octave above 250 Hz is…
Which bends around a pillar more easily?
qs.why: At 100 Hz the wavelength (≈3.4 m) is much larger than the pillar.

qs.q: 1 kHz has a wavelength of about…
Which type usually needs phantom power?
qs.why: Condenser capsules need a polarizing voltage and an internal preamp.

qs.q: A cardioid mic rejects most sound from…
qs.why: Point the rear at the thing you don't want.

qs.q: A singer moves right up to a cardioid mic. The tone usually gets…
A singer backs off from 5 cm to 10 cm. The level at the mic drops by about…
qs.why: Doubling distance, inverse-square estimate: about 6 dB.

qs.q: 29.97 fps equals…
qs.why: The 1.001 factor dates from NTSC color.

qs.q: At 50 fps, each frame lasts…
A 25 fps camera feeds a 59.94 switcher with no conversion. Most likely result?
o: Judder or no picture on that input
qs.why: The switcher can't use a signal it isn't running at, or has to repeat and drop frames.

qs.q: Which rate is associated with the film look?
qs.why: Cinema has used 24 fps for most of its history.

qs.q: UHD (3840×2160) has how many times the pixels of 1080p?
1920×1080 has what aspect ratio?
Does upscaling 720p to 1080p add real detail?
The “i” in 1080i means…
qs.why: Each frame is split into two interleaved fields.

qs.q: Changing the camera shutter speed makes the dark bands roll differently. Which problem is it?
qs.why: Shutter-dependent artifacts come from sampling the wall's pulsing.

qs.q: A wavy pattern changes when you pull focus. Which problem is it?
qs.why: Moiré depends on how the two pixel grids line up in the image.

qs.q: What causes moiré on an LED wall?
o: The sensor grid and the wall's pixel grid interfering
qs.why: Two fine grids beating against each other.

qs.q: First move when the wall looks wrong on camera?
qs.why: Discriminate between the two causes before fixing either.

Q-V4.title: Check · White balance and color temperature

qs.q: Which looks warmer?
A camera set for 5600 K shoots a stage lit at 3200 K. The picture looks…
qs.why: The camera expected bluer light, so the warm light looks even warmer.

qs.q: Why match white balance across cameras?
o: So cuts don't jump in color
qs.why: The audience notices color jumps between shots.

qs.q: Where should you set white balance?
qs.why: Balance to the light the camera will really see.

qs.q: Which light separates a person from the background?
qs.why: A back or rim light outlines the subject.

qs.q: Shadows are too harsh. The first thing to adjust is…
qs.why: Fill reduces the contrast the key creates.

qs.q: Light from directly overhead tends to…
qs.why: The brow blocks the light from the eye sockets.

qs.q: Which key:fill ratio looks more dramatic?
qs.why: More difference between key and fill = more contrast.

Q-L2.title: Check · Color temperature and color rendering

qs.q: Which is cooler (bluer)?
Why can an RGB-mixed “white” make skin look odd?
o: Its spectrum has gaps, so some colors render poorly
qs.why: Three narrow peaks leave parts of the spectrum missing.

qs.q: What does a color rendering metric describe?
o: How faithfully colors appear under the light
qs.why: It rates fidelity against a reference source.

qs.q: The kelvin unit is named after…
A 26° field at a 10 m throw is about how wide?
You double the throw distance. Illuminance becomes…
1 foot-candle is about…
qs.why: One lumen per square foot ≈ 10.76 lumens per square meter.

qs.q: Spreading the same fixture over a wider area makes it…
qs.why: The same light over more area.

qs.q: A 16-channel fixture starts at address 1. The next fixture should start at…
qs.why: It occupies 1–16, so the next free channel is 17.

qs.q: How many 16-channel fixtures fit in one universe?
Each DMX channel carries a value from…
You need to send one DMX line to two stage positions. You use…
qs.why: A splitter keeps each branch a proper line.

Q-A5.title: Check · Feedback and gain before feedback

qs.q: Feedback begins when the loop gain at some frequency reaches about…
qs.why: At unity, each trip round the loop is as loud as the last, so it sustains.

qs.q: The pastor steps from 30 cm to 15 cm from the mic. Roughly how much more gain before feedback?
qs.why: Half the distance, about 6 dB more of the pastor at the mic (inverse-square estimate).

qs.q: You open four mics instead of two. Gain before feedback changes by about…
qs.why: Each doubling of open mics costs about 3 dB.

qs.q: Which is the LAST thing to reach for?
o: Aim the mic's null at the wedge

Q-A6.title: Check · Digital audio: samples, bits and delay

qs.q: At 48 kHz, the highest frequency the system can represent is about…
qs.why: Half the sample rate: the Nyquist limit.

qs.q: Each extra bit of depth adds about…
qs.why: 20·log10(2) ≈ 6 dB of dynamic range per bit.

qs.q: A 10 ms delay is roughly equivalent to sound traveling…
Two digital devices click every few seconds when connected. A likely cause is…
qs.why: Unsynchronized clocks drift and slip samples.

qs.q: The pastor's wireless drops out only at the far left of the stage. First suspect?
o: The radio path: antennas, line of sight, reflections
qs.why: Position-dependent dropouts point at the radio link.

qs.q: A diversity receiver…
o: Uses two antennas and picks the better signal
qs.why: Two antennas rarely fade at the same moment.

qs.q: Intermodulation means…
o: Transmitters mixing to create new frequencies that can land on other channels
qs.why: Why every frequency needs coordinating as a set.

qs.q: Where should you test a wireless mic before service?
o: From where it will actually be used
qs.why: Test the path the way it will be used.

qs.q: A camera sits 40 m from the switcher. Which is the more reliable choice?
o: A 40 m passive consumer display cable
qs.why: Use a transport built for the distance.

qs.q: Picture at the wall plate; no picture at the patch panel. The fault is…
o: Between the wall plate and the patch

qs.q: What does fiber add besides distance?
Video over IP needs…
qs.why: Video can fill a network fast.

Q-V6.title: Check · LED walls on camera: timing and standards

qs.q: Your cameras run at 59.94p. The wall processor says 50 Hz. What's wrong?
o: The wall and cameras are in different frame-rate families
qs.why: A standards mismatch: fix the odd one out, not the whole building.

qs.q: You switch the shutter from 1/100 to 1/60 at 59.94p and the bands disappear. Why?
o: Each frame now captures whole cycles of the wall's light
qs.why: Whole cycles per frame means every frame gets the same light.

qs.q: You set the shutter to 1/1000. The bands most likely…
qs.why: A shorter exposure samples a smaller slice of the pulsing.

qs.q: The wall is dimmed to 10% for a candle moment and a faint band returns. Best live move?
o: Cut to a shot without the wall
qs.why: Protect the room; change the shot.

Q-V7.title: Check · Streaming: codecs, bitrate and delay

qs.q: Which scene is hardest to compress at a fixed bitrate?
o: Haze and moving lights over a crowd
A locked-off shot of the pulpit
qs.why: Lots of fine, changing detail costs bits.

qs.q: Your stream needs 6 Mbit/s. Which upload is the safer plan?
qs.why: Headroom for peaks and other traffic (illustrative numbers).

qs.q: Why is the overflow room's lobby TV behind the room?
o: The stream adds seconds of delay
qs.why: Encoding, buffering and delivery add delay.

qs.q: What does a codec do?
o: Compresses video to fit a bitrate

qs.q: Red light + green light make…
Why does a deep blue gel make a fixture much dimmer?
o: It removes most of the light that isn't blue

qs.q: Red + green + blue light, balanced, make…
A saturated blue wash looks blocky on the stream. What do you check first?
o: How the look reads on camera
qs.why: Some colors are hard on camera channels and compression.

qs.q: Why can a stage look fine to the eye and bad on camera?
qs.why: The eye adapts; the sensor clips.

qs.q: A fixture flickers only on camera at low intensity. A likely cause?
o: Its output pulses and the camera samples it

qs.q: Which tool shows consistent key light across the stage?
o: A light meter or camera waveform

qs.q: Cameras should be white-balanced to…
o: The white chosen for faces on stage
qs.why: Balance to the light that's really on the people.

qs.q: 30 fixtures × 40 channels. How many universes?
A node…
o: Converts network lighting data back to DMX lines

qs.q: RDM lets the console…
o: Discover and address fixtures over the DMX line
qs.why: Two-way management over the same line.

qs.q: Where should lighting network traffic live?
o: On a planned lighting network with an owner

qs.q: On an unmanaged switch, multicast video goes…
o: Only to the display that asked

qs.q: What lets a managed switch send multicast only to ports that asked?
qs.why: The switch listens to membership requests.

qs.q: A VLAN…
o: Logically separates traffic on shared switches

qs.q: The office network is down to one free port. You…
At 120 V, a 1,200 W load draws about…
Who resets a tripped breaker in a locked electrical room?
qs.why: Know the arithmetic; know whose door it is.

qs.q: A UPS is for…
o: Riding through short outages and shutting down cleanly

qs.q: Amplifiers should be powered…
Why couldn't EQ fix all ten seats?
o: The notches sit at different frequencies at each seat
qs.why: An EQ applies to every seat at once.

qs.q: Which test could have proved the reflection idea WRONG?
o: Turning the fill down and seeing no change in the notches
qs.why: State the result that would falsify you before testing.

qs.q: Who re-aims an overhead loudspeaker?
o: The installer's qualified crew with a lift and an exclusion zone
qs.why: Overhead work belongs to a qualified crew.

qs.q: What did the fix cost?
qs.why: Every coverage fix moves the problem somewhere; name where.

qs.q: Why did last week's cut “work”?
Where was the first failure?
What does proximity effect do?
o: Adds low end up close on directional mics

qs.q: The workflow fix was…
o: Line check at the loudest line, real distance
qs.why: Test the way it will be used.

qs.q: The WORSHIP preset opened the wrong mics because…
qs.why: The preset recalled numbers; the world changed.

qs.q: What made the fix provable?
After the fix, you should test…
qs.why: Every preset, every output that matters.

qs.q: When should a change be logged?
Fixtures 3 through 8 flicker; 1 and 2 are steady. Where do you look first?
qs.why: The first failing fixture marks the spot.

qs.q: Which is NOT a common physical cause?
qs.why: Color temperature isn't a data fault.

qs.q: Console output is steady on a tester. That tells you…
Elias won't sign because…
o: There's no evidence against a stated requirement
qs.why: A signature is a claim about evidence.

qs.q: The bands disappear when you change the shutter. That tells you the problem is…
What put the processor back to 50 Hz on Christmas Eve?
o: A factory reset during a tile swap
qs.why: What changed? The rental tech's reset.

qs.q: Which move fixes moiré on Cam 2?
o: Focus on the people, not the wall
qs.why: Moiré is spatial: focus, zoom, angle.

qs.q: Best place to keep the rental's settings?
o: Taped to the processor and in the log
qs.why: The rental doesn't remember them for you.

qs.q: Which four disciplines does the Fieldbook say make one AV experience?
qs.why: Sound, picture and light ride on computers, networks and infrastructure. A weak link in any one of them breaks the experience.

qs.q: The console meter is moving. What have you proved?
o: That the signal reaches the console — not that people hear it
qs.why: Verify the last mile: check at the loudspeaker, the screen and the stream return.

qs.q: Every source needs an owner, a destination and…
qs.why: Route with intent. If nobody can say why a signal goes somewhere, nobody will notice when it stops.

qs.q: A 1,000 Mb/s link carries 850 Mb/s. What is its utilization?

Q-FB2.title: Check · What sound is — and why it gets quieter

qs.q: Frequency is…
o: How many waves pass per second — heard as pitch
qs.why: Frequency is measured in hertz (waves per second). Loudness is amplitude, measured in decibels.

qs.q: Roughly how long is a 50 Hz wave in air?
qs.why: λ = 343 ÷ 50 ≈ 6.86 m. Low notes are room-sized.

qs.q: A reading is 92 dB at 5 m. About what should it be at 10 m in open air?
qs.why: Doubling the distance costs about 6 dB: 92 − 6 = 86 dB.

qs.q: Why not judge the mix only from the booth?
o: The booth is rarely a typical seat — check where people sit
qs.why: Measure and listen in several seats. Distance and reflections change what each seat hears.

Q-FB3.title: Check · The frequency spectrum and EQ

qs.q: A high-pass filter set at 100 Hz on a vocal…
o: Removes rumble below about 100 Hz and lets higher frequencies through
qs.why: High frequencies pass; the lows below the cutoff are reduced.

qs.q: The vocal sounds muddy and boxy. Where do you look first?
qs.why: Mud and boxiness live in the low mids. Cut there a little before adding anything.

qs.q: What is one octave above 250 Hz?
qs.why: An octave doubles the frequency: 2 × 250 = 500 Hz.

qs.q: Why compare with the EQ bypassed?
o: To hear whether the change actually helped
qs.why: Ears adapt quickly. Bypass is a before/after test.

Q-FB4.title: Check · Gain structure, noise and hum

qs.q: Where is gain set?
qs.why: Gain happens early; mixing happens later.

qs.q: A voice arrives at −34 dBFS and the target is −18 dBFS. How much gain do you add?
A hum starts when the laptop is plugged into the console. What is the safe first move?
o: Remove the ground pin from the laptop's plug
Isolate the signal (a DI box or isolator) and tell whoever owns the power — never defeat a protective earth
qs.why: Hum is fixed on the signal side or by the electrician. The earth is there to protect people.

qs.q: Why do balanced cables reject noise?
o: Noise lands on both conductors equally and cancels when the inverted copy is flipped back
qs.why: Common-mode noise cancels at a balanced input.

Q-FB5.title: Check · The channel strip, the stagebox and the label

qs.q: Phantom power is for…
o: Condenser microphones — 48 V sent down a balanced cable
qs.why: Condensers need it; on a correctly wired balanced line, a dynamic mic simply doesn't use it.

qs.q: Every stage input drops at the same moment. What do you suspect first?
o: The digital snake between the stagebox and the console
qs.why: Everything at once points to a shared path, not to 32 separate faults.

qs.q: The channel's CLIP light is on. What is too high?
qs.why: The meter reads after the preamp, so reduce the gain there.

qs.q: Why label both ends of a cable?
o: So the person at either end can find the other end without guessing
qs.why: Labels are evidence for the next person — which is why they have to be true.

Q-FB6.title: Check · Electricity basics — and whose panel it is

qs.q: By Ohm's law, a 2 A current through 3 Ω drops how many volts?
A 1,200 W load on 120 V draws…
The same breaker trips twice during rehearsal. What do you do?
o: Stop, reduce the load if that's safe to do, and call the electrician — the panel is theirs
Swap it with a bigger breaker
Tape it in the on position
qs.why: A trip is the protection doing its job. Diagnosis and repair belong to the electrician.

qs.q: Why are large systems powered up in sequence?
o: To avoid inrush current tripping breakers and loudspeakers popping
qs.why: Staggering start-up spreads the surges out; amplifiers go on last and off first.

qs.q: Which pattern rejects sound from directly behind?
qs.why: A cardioid's null is at the rear — aim it at the wedge.

qs.q: The reader moves from 5 cm to 20 cm from the mic. About how much quieter is her voice?
Which mic needs phantom power?
qs.why: Condensers need a polarizing supply; phantom sends it down the cable.

qs.q: Nobody can hear the reading. What is the first fix?
o: Get the mic closer to the reader and aim it at the mouth
qs.why: Fix it at the source. Every doubling of distance you remove gives back about 6 dB.

Q-FB8.title: Check · Video basics — frames, formats and the house standard

qs.q: At 59.94 frames per second, how long does each frame last?
How many pixels are in a 1920 × 1080 frame?
A new camera shows black on the switcher but works on its own monitor. What do you check first?
o: Update the switcher firmware during the service
Its output format against the switcher's house standard
qs.why: Resolution, frame-rate family and scan type all have to match.

qs.q: Why does interlaced video comb on motion?
o: Each frame is two fields captured at different moments
qs.why: The two halves of the frame show the subject in two slightly different places.

Q-FB9.title: Check · Readiness — maintenance, computers and the register

qs.q: A 2 Ah pack powers a 0.4 A transmitter. What is the ideal runtime?
qs.why: t = 2 ÷ 0.4 = 5 h — real packs give less.

qs.q: Which of these belongs in an asset register?
o: Location, age, firmware, license and expiry date
qs.why: You can't budget replacements you haven't listed.

qs.q: When is the right time for a big software update?
o: After the service, with a rollback plan and a known-good version kept
qs.why: Update when there's time to test, and with a way back.

qs.q: What is a backup you've never restored from?
o: Only fine if it's in the cloud
qs.why: A backup is only evidence once you have restored from it.

Q-FB10.title: Check · Lighting basics and DMX addressing

qs.q: A 16-channel fixture starts at address 33. What is its last channel?
How many 12-channel fixtures fit in one universe?
Every fixture after number 6 flickers. Where do you look?
o: The link into and out of fixture 6
qs.why: A daisy chain fails downstream of the bad link.

qs.q: Why terminate the last fixture?
o: So the fixture can turn on
To stop the signal reflecting back and corrupting the data
qs.why: A terminator absorbs the signal at the end of the line.

Q-FB11.title: Check · Something broke during the service — now what?

qs.q: Something fails mid-service. What is the first step after staying calm?
o: Replace the device nearest to you
Find out whose fault it is
qs.why: You can't isolate what you haven't named.

qs.q: You made three changes at once and now it works. What's the problem?
o: The log will be too long
You don't know which change fixed it
qs.why: One change at a time keeps the cause visible.

qs.q: According to the reliability mindset, where do live systems usually fail?
o: At interfaces — connectors, power, RF, network and hand-offs
qs.why: Trace energy, data and control across every junction.

qs.q: A workaround saved the service. What happens next?
o: Write it down and schedule the real fix
qs.why: An unwritten workaround turns into technical debt.

qs.q: Roughly how long is a quarter-wave antenna for 600 MHz?
Why can't last tour's frequency plan be reused everywhere?
o: Local services and other users are different in each place

qs.q: Receivers stacked beside the LED wall keep dropping out. What is the first fix?
o: Move the receivers away from the wall and use external antennas with line of sight
qs.why: The Fieldbook case: it's not the mic — it's the environment, the placement and RF physics.

qs.q: What is the best battery practice?
o: Fresh batteries checked before every show, with spares ready
Batteries don't matter on new systems
qs.why: A dying battery looks like an RF problem at the worst moment.

Q-FB13.title: Check · Phase and time — when two copies meet

qs.q: A delay tower is 17 m from the mains. About how much delay does it need?
A guitar sounds thin when both of its mics are up. What do you check first?
o: The phase and polarity between the two mics
qs.why: Two mics at different distances mean two arrival times, so some frequencies cancel.

qs.q: Why does a diversity receiver have two antennas?
o: They are unlikely to both be in a multipath null at once
qs.why: Nulls are local; two positions give the receiver a choice.

qs.q: What does swapping pins 2 and 3 in one cable cause?
qs.why: Same signal, flipped upside down — it cancels against a correct copy.

Q-FB14.title: Check · Fixtures, angles, and key, fill and back

qs.q: A 25° fixture is 5 m from the stage. How wide is the pool?
The presenter's eye sockets look dark. What is the light probably doing?
o: Coming mostly from overhead — add a key light about 45° in front
qs.why: Top light alone makes raccoon eyes.

qs.q: Which fixture throws a hard-edged gobo pattern?
qs.why: Ellipsoidals have focusable lenses and shutters for sharp edges.

qs.q: The director wants a new hanging point tonight. Who decides?
o: The rigger and structural engineer, with a plan and a rating
qs.why: Anything overhead belongs to them. Nobody improvises it.

Q-FB15.title: Check · Scenes, snapshots and the change freeze

qs.q: What does a “safe” do on a console?
o: Protects selected channels from being changed by a scene recall
qs.why: Recall what you mean to, and protect what must not move.

qs.q: The control software lost the switcher, but program video is still running. Which plane failed?
qs.why: Video is still flowing; only the way you command it is gone.

qs.q: When should a firmware update happen?
o: After the event, with a rollback plan and a known-good version
qs.why: The change freeze protects the show.

qs.q: Which of these is a non-software fallback for stage lighting?
o: Climbing to switch a fixture on by hand
A console preset or the house lights at a safe level
Buying a new license during the show
qs.why: Keep a fallback that doesn't need software — and nobody climbs during a show.

qs.q: A singer's wedge changes whenever the engineer rides her channel fader. What's wrong?
o: The monitor send is post-fader — it should be pre-fader
qs.why: Monitors use pre-fader sends so mix moves don't change what's on stage.

qs.q: What does a DCA do?
o: Sends a mix to a wedge
Controls the volume of many channels without changing their sends

qs.q: What should a mix-minus for a remote guest contain?
o: Everything except the guest's own voice
qs.why: Their own voice returning late makes them stumble.

qs.q: Where do effects sends usually tap?
o: Post-fader, so reverb follows the channel level
qs.why: Pull the vocal down and its reverb comes down with it.

Q-FB17.title: Check · Room physics — the room is part of the signal chain

qs.q: A room is 7 m long. Where is its lowest length mode?
A room has V = 1,000 m³ and A = 200 m². What is its RT60?
Why do bass notes bend around a pillar when high notes don't?
qs.why: Objects much smaller than the wavelength hardly block it.

qs.q: The left side is boomy and the right is thin. What do you do first?
o: Measure several seats and look at where the sources stack up
qs.why: Find the cause in the room and on the stage before you EQ the symptom.

qs.q: The stream measures −19 LUFS and the target is −14 LUFS. What correction does it need?
Why give the stream its own mix?
o: Listeners on phones hear a different room from the people in the seats
qs.why: Same sources, different destination, different processing.

qs.q: Why shouldn't you slam a limiter on the stream mix?
o: The platform compresses again, and it gets squashed and lifeless

qs.q: The recording sounds squashed and hard to edit. What's the fix?
o: Record at a lower sample rate
Record clean stems before the stream processing
qs.why: CASE-008: one processed mix for the stream, a separate clean recording.

Q-FB19.title: Check · Getting the picture there — HDMI, SDI, IP, fiber

qs.q: How much active picture is 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, 10-bit, 4:2:2 (s = 2)?
The main camera vanishes from the switcher, but its own monitor still shows a picture. What do you test next?
o: The cable path, segment by segment
qs.why: It's a signal path failure, not a camera failure.

qs.q: What is the cliff effect?
o: Digital video is fine until it fails suddenly, with little warning
qs.why: Marginal cables pass, and then they don't.

qs.q: Which transport locks in place and runs long distances in live production?

Q-FB20.title: Check · Addresses, subnets and the IP plan

qs.q: How many usable host addresses does a /24 subnet have?
qs.why: 2⁸ − 2 = 254 (the network and broadcast addresses aren't usable).

qs.q: The console is 198.18.0.20/24 and the stagebox is 198.18.1.20/24. What's wrong?
qs.why: The third number differs, so with /24 they aren't local to each other.

qs.q: Why use a static address or a reservation for the console?
o: So its address doesn't change between shows
qs.why: Control apps and remote panels look for it at one address.

qs.q: A remote panel won't connect. What do you check first?
o: Power and link lights, then the subnet

Q-FB21.title: Check · Dynamics — compressors, gates, limiters and effects

qs.q: Threshold −20 dB, ratio 4:1, input −4 dB. What is the output before makeup gain?
The kick lost all its punch after compression. What is the likely cause?
qs.why: A fast attack flattens the transient that carries the punch.

qs.q: What does a gate do on a tom mic?
o: It closes between hits to cut bleed
qs.why: Below the threshold, the gate turns the channel down.

qs.q: What does pre-delay on a vocal reverb do?
o: It keeps the words clear before the reverb blooms
qs.why: A short gap separates the dry consonants from the tail.

Q-FB22.title: Check · Computers in AV — accounts, updates and habits

qs.q: How much entropy does a 12-character password drawn from 26 lowercase letters have?
The room computer suddenly plays no audio. What is the quick check?
qs.why: Updates and docking often change the default device.

qs.q: Why does a meeting room sign in with its own account?
o: So a policy written for people doesn't sign the room out
qs.why: Identity is part of the room's signal path.

qs.q: What does RAM hold?
qs.why: Storage keeps files; RAM is the desk you work on.

Q-FB23.title: Check · DSP fundamentals — filters, Q and slopes

qs.q: A cut is centered at 1 kHz and is 250 Hz wide. What is its Q?
A narrow whine sits at 3.2 kHz. Which filter do you use?
qs.why: Remove the problem without taking the whole region with it.

qs.q: What does the slope of a filter describe?
o: How steeply it cuts beyond the cutoff (dB per octave)

qs.q: What is the cost of a linear-phase FIR filter?
qs.why: Look-ahead takes time — it matters for live monitors.

Q-FB24.title: Check · A meeting room is four disciplines

qs.q: A camera works in one room but not in an identical room down the hall. What do you suspect?
o: Inconsistent room configuration — compare it against the standard
qs.why: Identical on paper isn't identical in fact.

qs.q: Which discipline does DNS belong to?
Why keep a written room standard?
o: So every room behaves the same way and differences stand out
qs.why: Standards turn a hundred mysteries into one.

qs.q: What should room monitoring measure?
o: What the user experiences — can a call start with sound and picture?
Only whether devices respond to a ping
qs.why: A green ping can hide a silent room.

Q-FB25.title: Check · The OSI model, AV style

qs.q: A device is in the wrong VLAN. Which layer is that?
qs.why: VLANs separate traffic at the switch.

qs.q: Why does live media usually ride on UDP?
o: No retransmission delays — late packets are useless anyway
qs.why: For live audio and video, on time beats complete.

qs.q: The room says “login expired.” Which layer?
qs.why: Starting and keeping the conversation is the session layer.

qs.q: Where do you start troubleshooting?

Q-FB26.title: Check · Latency — every stage adds some

qs.q: Stages add 3, 120, 40, 60 and 25 ms. What is the total latency?
In that chain, where would you look first to cut the delay?
o: The 120 ms stage — the biggest term
qs.why: Shrinking the biggest term pays most.

qs.q: Which kind of latency decides whether people talk over each other on a call?
qs.why: Your words go there, and their reply comes back.

qs.q: Which change usually lowers latency?
o: Wired instead of wireless, with fewer processing stages
qs.why: Every stage you remove is time you get back.

Q-FB27.title: Check · Everything becomes numbers — binary, control and macros

qs.q: What is the theoretical dynamic range of 24-bit audio?
A stream looks blocky whenever there's fast motion. What is the likely cause?
o: The bitrate is too low for the content
qs.why: Motion needs more data per second.

qs.q: A macro runs perfectly in rehearsal but breaks the room when a call is already live. Why?
o: It assumes a room state that wasn't true
qs.why: Macros replay steps; they don't check the state first.

qs.q: A touch-panel button press is…
o: An analog voltage sent to the projector
Data — a command to a control processor
qs.why: Control is small data, but it is data.

Q-FB28.title: Check · Coverage and intelligibility — point it at people

qs.q: A reflection arrives 2.5 ms after the direct sound. Where is the first notch?
A loudspeaker has 92 dB sensitivity (1 W, 1 m) and 50 W of power. About what level reaches 8 m?
Why does a ceiling-aimed fill hurt the center seats most?
o: They're too close to the mains
They get the direct sound and the late ceiling reflection at similar levels, so they comb-filter
qs.why: Similar-level arrivals, different times, notches in speech.

qs.q: When should accessibility be designed in?
o: From the start — listening systems, captions, readable screens
qs.why: It's part of the standard, not a patch.

Q-FB29.title: Check · Operations — roles, hand-offs and “write it down”

qs.q: A ticket is closed with “fixed.” What's missing?
o: What was wrong, what was done, and how it was verified
qs.why: The next person needs the cause and the proof.

qs.q: What makes a good hand-off?
o: State, open issues and the next step — said plainly
qs.why: Hand-offs are an interface, and interfaces fail.

qs.q: Why does the Fieldbook ask leaders for the run of show the night before?
o: Better preparation means a calmer service with fewer surprises
qs.why: Readiness starts upstream of the booth.

qs.q: “If it's not documented, it doesn't exist” protects…
o: The next person, who wasn't in the room
qs.why: Knowledge in one head is a single point of failure.

Q-FB30.title: Check · Network reliability for AV — VLANs, QoS and multicast

qs.q: A 1 Gb/s uplink carries 780 Mb/s. What is its utilization?
Multicast audio floods every port and the meeting rooms slow down. What is probably missing?
qs.why: Snooping lets the switch send multicast only where it's wanted.

qs.q: Which traffic gets the highest QoS priority for live AV?
qs.why: It's the least tolerant of delay and loss.

qs.q: You think a switch setting is wrong on the corporate network. What do you do?
o: Bring evidence to the network owner and let them change it
qs.why: The network owner owns the network.

Q-FB31.title: Check · Picture and light on camera

qs.q: What shutter speed does the rule of thumb give at 25 fps?
A key light gives 900 lux at 3 m. It's moved to 6 m. About how much light reaches the subject now?
The picture is noisy in a dim room. What should you change before raising the gain?
o: Add light, or open the aperture
qs.why: Gain brightens the noise too; light and aperture don't.

qs.q: The CEO's face shows rolling bands on camera. What is the likely cause?
o: LED flicker from PWM dimming beating against the shutter
qs.why: Test the lights with the real cameras; adjust the shutter or the dimming.

qs.q: Why did the room lean left before the mix even started?
o: Most of the low-end sources were stacked on audience-left
qs.why: Energy piles up where the sources are.

qs.q: “Mix the source, not just the board” means…
o: Set the stage amps and instruments right, because the console can't turn them down
qs.why: A loud amp on stage reaches the room directly.

qs.q: A new wedge aimed at the left wall made things worse. Why?
o: It became another loudspeaker for the already-loud side of the room
qs.why: Aim monitors at the performer, not at the room's walls.

qs.q: What is the best first step in a room that sounds uneven?
o: Measure several seats with the same material
qs.why: Evidence from many seats before any fix.

qs.q: Why is one dim module so obvious to the audience?
o: Eyes judge brightness by contrast with the neighboring modules
LED walls are always too bright
qs.why: Contrast sensitivity makes one square stand out.

qs.q: What should you check first, without touching the wall?
o: Climb up to reseat the cable
The processor's status for that module: data, power, temperature
qs.why: Evidence first — nobody works at height mid-show.

qs.q: While you wait for the fix, how do you protect the message?
o: Move the lyrics and captions away from the dim square

qs.q: It's raining and the vendor wants to open the wall. Who decides when?
o: The weather plan and the vendor's safety plan
qs.why: Physical work in weather belongs to the owner's plan.

qs.q: Stage control is lost mid-service. Which is a safe live fallback?
o: Climb to switch on a truss light
House lights to a readable level and a preset that doesn't need the software
Unplug the interface and plug it back in repeatedly
qs.why: Stay on the ground, and don't gamble the rest of the service.

qs.q: What prevents this failure?
o: Licenses with expiry dates in the asset register, and reminders sent to two people
qs.why: An expiry nobody tracks is a failure with a date on it.

qs.q: Why did SIGNAL change the Fieldbook's climb?
o: The truss was too high for the story
Overhead work belongs to trained crew with equipment and a plan — never during a live event
qs.why: The lesson stays; the unsafe act doesn't.

qs.q: When should the software be updated?
o: After the service, from a known-good installer, and tested
qs.why: Update when there's time to prove it.

qs.q: Why did the camera come back after a replug?
o: Replugging forced the camera to enumerate again, and the software found it
qs.why: A workaround, not a fix — and the evidence that the user wasn't the cause.

qs.q: What turned 37 “user error” tickets into one problem?
o: Asking the users to be careful
Grouping them by room type and extender, then reading the logs
qs.why: Patterns live across tickets, not inside one.

qs.q: How do you prove the fix?
o: Reproduce the idle that caused the drop, before and after the change
qs.why: A fix is proven when the trigger no longer causes the failure.

qs.q: Why did the software lose the camera for good?
o: It came back as a new device, and the software kept looking for the old one
qs.why: Selecting the camera by type, not by instance, fixes that part.

qs.q: Why didn't the backup reference save the picture?
o: It followed the main, so it drifted with it
qs.why: Dependence on the thing you back up isn't redundancy.

qs.q: Who fixes the damaged antenna cable on the roof?
qs.why: Boundaries hold even an hour before air.

qs.q: What makes a backup reference independent?
o: It sits in a different rack
It has its own timing source and doesn't follow the main
qs.why: Independence is about what it depends on, not where it sits.

qs.q: How was the fix proven?
o: Ten stable minutes watched on the gateway and the program return
qs.why: Stability over time, where the picture goes.

qs.q: Last tour's frequency plan worked for eighteen months. What is it in a new city?
o: A hypothesis to check against a scan and local use
qs.why: It was proven somewhere else. Each city's radio environment is different.

qs.q: Received signal −70 dBm, noise floor −100 dBm (illustrative). The margin is…
Why coordinate sixteen channels as one set?
o: Transmitters can combine into new frequencies that hit other channels
qs.why: Intermodulation: the set matters, not just each channel.

qs.q: A quarter-wave antenna at an illustrative 600 MHz is about…
qs.why: λ = 3×10⁸ ÷ 6×10⁸ = 0.5 m; a quarter is 0.125 m.

Q-P2.title: Check · Temporary power: who connects what

qs.q: Venue 2's power drawing is ten years old. You…
o: Ask for today's service, the drawing date and whose electrician makes the tie-in
qs.why: An old drawing is a question to ask.

qs.q: Who makes the connection between the generator and the venue's system?
o: A qualified electrician from the venue or the power vendor

qs.q: A distro rated for 32 A per circuit at 230 V (illustrative) can carry about…
qs.why: 230 × 32 ≈ 7,360 W, before any planning margin the electrician sets.

qs.q: The generator shows an alarm mid-show. Your first move?
o: Call the power vendor and protect the show

qs.q: A diversity receiver…
o: Uses two antennas in different places and takes the better signal
qs.why: Two places rarely fade at the same instant.

qs.q: Both antennas sit behind a steel frame. Diversity will…
o: Pick the better of two weak signals — still weak
qs.why: Diversity can't create line of sight.

qs.q: Why can turning away from the antennas cause a drop?
o: The body absorbs radio between transmitter and antenna

qs.q: The best test for a position-dependent drop is…
o: A bench test at the booth
A walk test along the real path, facing the real way, with a meter
qs.why: Test the path the way the show uses it.

qs.q: Why couldn't diversity save channel 7 at the lip?
o: Both antennas were behind the same steel frame
qs.why: Two weak signals are still weak.

qs.q: Why not change the frequency?
o: No interference was measured; it hides the evidence and fixes nothing
qs.why: Change what the evidence points at.

qs.q: Who approves the new antenna mount?
qs.why: Anything mounted on structure goes through its owner.

qs.q: What proves the fix?
o: The receiver's meter at the booth
A walk test with Marisol at every position, before and after
qs.why: Prove it along the real path.

qs.q: The house crew chief says, “We've hung heavier from that beam before.” That is…
o: Good enough for a light load
qs.why: Past loads say nothing certain about today's beam, configuration or condition.

qs.q: Which belongs in a rigging plan?
o: What hangs where, its weight, what it hangs from, each point's rating, who signed
qs.why: Plans are documents people can check.

qs.q: Who approves loads on a building's structure?
o: A structural engineer, with the venue's data
qs.why: The head rigger owns the plan; the engineer approves the structure.

qs.q: There's no rating and no time to get one. The right move is…
o: Change the design: approved positions, checked ground support, or cut
qs.why: Half of unknown is still unknown.

Q-N2.title: Check · Show networks on the road

qs.q: Common copper network cable is limited to about…
qs.why: About 100 m between active devices; beyond that, fiber or another switch.

qs.q: Lights go wrong on one fixture type only; everything else on the same network is perfect. The network is…
qs.why: A network fault wouldn't pick one fixture type and one kind of cue.

qs.q: When should you test your backup path?
qs.why: Redundancy you haven't tested is a hope.

qs.q: The venue offers to link your show network to theirs “for convenience”. You…
o: Keep the show network separate; their network has an owner

qs.q: Why did cue 14 snap?
o: The update reset the show's default fade time, and cue 14 used the default

qs.q: Why were the moving heads aimed low?
o: The update replaced their fixture profile, so stored values meant different angles

qs.q: Who decides whether to stop the show?
qs.why: The booth reports; the SM decides.

qs.q: What proves the fix?
o: A full cue-to-cue against the rehearsal record

Q-C1.title: Check · Room combining and control states

qs.q: The airwall is closed but the panel says COMBINED. What does the system believe?
qs.why: The panel shows the system's belief, which comes from the sensor. Here the sensor and the wall disagree.

qs.q: Room A plays Room B's emcee and ignores Room A's own mic. Most likely state?
o: COMBINED while the wall is closed
qs.why: In COMBINED, one room's inputs feed every zone; the other room's plates are ignored (in this model).

qs.q: Who reconnects a hotel's airwall sensor or overrides its interlock?
qs.why: It's the hotel's system. Use the panel as a user; the configuration and overrides belong to its owner.

qs.q: Why feed both wall plates before a planned state change?
o: So the program is present in either state — make before break
qs.why: A state flip is instant. If your signal is already on the right path for the new state, nobody hears the switch.

Q-V8.title: Check · Streaming tap points and A/V sync

qs.q: The room engineer mutes a mic, but the stream still carries it. The stream's tap is most likely…
o: At the channel input, before the mute
qs.why: An input tap sits before processing, mute and fader, so it hears everything.

qs.q: Why is a post-fader stream mix often wrong in a small room with a loud band?
o: The room mix carries little band because the room hears them acoustically
qs.why: The PA only supplies what the room lacks. The stream has no acoustic band.

qs.q: Video lags audio by 3 frames at 59.94 fps (≈50 ms) and audio has 10 ms of its own latency. How much audio delay?
Best proof the stream sounds right?
o: A second listener on cellular with headphones, on the real stream
qs.why: Independent path, where the viewers are.

qs.q: The stream heard a mic the room engineer had muted. Why?
o: The stems were tapped at the input, before the mute
qs.why: Tap point decides what the stream hears.

qs.q: Why did moving the stems post-fader lose the band?
o: The room's balance barely includes a band the room hears acoustically
qs.why: A room mix isn't a stream mix.

qs.q: Picture is 50 ms late, audio 10 ms. Delay the audio by…
An independent-path proof means…
o: A phone on cellular, headphones, the real stream
qs.why: Not sharing the path you're proving.

Q-L8.title: Check · Show control, cue lists and change freezes

qs.q: Who calls “go” on a cue during the show?
qs.why: The stage manager calls the show.

qs.q: After the freeze, the client asks for a different music track. You…
o: Log it; if the stage manager holds and it can be tested, maybe; otherwise tomorrow
qs.why: A freeze is a rule with a door in it: the stage manager's hold and a test.

qs.q: The checklist ran at 5:30; the room flipped for dinner at 5:40. What do you rerun?
o: Source and floor checks — anything the flip could touch
qs.why: A check proves the state at the time you ran it.

qs.q: Why is show control a risk as well as a help?
o: One untested GO can misfire several departments at once

qs.q: Viewfinder fine, router correct, switcher black. Next?
o: Walk a field monitor down the path
qs.why: Find the last good and first bad point.

qs.q: Picture on the camera side of the pocket, none on the house side. The fault is…
qs.why: Between last good and first bad.

qs.q: Who opens the power side of a floor pocket?
When should source checks run?
o: After the last room change, then freeze
qs.why: A check proves the state at the time you ran it.

Q-N3.title: Check · Addressing, DHCP and fixed addresses

qs.q: A scanner is connected, has a valid address, but its gateway is a router with no internet. What happens?
o: It looks connected and reaches nothing outside
qs.why: The gateway is the door out. Wrong door, no way out.

qs.q: Two DHCP servers on one network, not coordinated. A device asks for an address. It gets…
Where should a fixed address for an encoder go?
o: Outside the DHCP pool, or reserved in the server
qs.why: Otherwise the server may hand it out again.

qs.q: Why do two networks you join often overlap?
qs.why: Millions of networks use the same few private blocks.

Q-A10.title: Check · Mix-minus, IFB and in-ear monitoring

qs.q: Why is an in-ear failure so disruptive for a performer?
o: The in-ear mix is nearly all they can hear
qs.why: Isolation is the point — and the risk.

qs.q: A mix-minus for a remote presenter contains…
FOH loses stage-box control for seconds at a time. What protects the headliner's ears?
o: Monitor control moved to the planned local fallback mixer at the stage
qs.why: A local path a network drop can't reach.

qs.q: During a hold, what does the stage manager need from audio?
o: A working announce mic and talkback to the performers' ears
qs.why: Communication is the show during a hold.

qs.q: Twelve rooms show “sign-in failed · password expired”. A personal laptop joins the same call from the same room. The cause most likely lives in…
qs.why: The laptop proves the service and the path; the error names the account.

qs.q: Why can't a room simply “change its password” when a policy asks it to?
o: Nobody is there to choose, type and store a new secret — and it isn't AV's decision anyway
qs.why: A room account needs a managed credential, not a person.

qs.q: Every room shares one password written on a note. The risk is…
o: One leak opens every room's calendar, camera and microphones
qs.why: Blast radius: shared secrets fail together.

qs.q: Who decides to move room accounts to a different policy?
o: The identity / security team that owns the accounts
Whoever has an admin console open
qs.why: Access decisions belong to security; AV brings evidence and verifies.

qs.q: Remote participants hear themselves echo from your room. Where is the leak?
qs.why: The echo returns through the room whose mics picked up the far end's voice: yours.

qs.q: What does an echo canceller need to work?
o: The exact signal sent to the loudspeakers, as a reference
qs.why: It predicts the echo from the reference and subtracts it.

qs.q: The room processor cancels echo well. An update turns on the conferencing software's canceller too. Likely result?
o: Two cancellers fight; bursts of echo or chopped voices

qs.q: Turning the room's microphone gain down 10 dB will…
o: Make everyone quieter, echo included, without changing the path

Q-CASE-013.title: Check · The Room That Hears Twice

qs.q: Why did the Harbor Room start echoing on a Monday?
o: Sunday's update switched on a second canceller
qs.why: An update restored a setting nobody expected it to touch.

qs.q: Which canceller should stay on?
o: The room processor's — nearest the mics, with the true reference
qs.why: One canceller, the one that can see the loudspeaker signal.

qs.q: How do you make the fix survive the next update?
o: Put it in the managed room profile and add a post-update echo check
qs.why: Blocking updates would create an exception room.

qs.q: Mid-call, your room hears itself. That means…
o: The far end's room is returning your audio
qs.why: Echo is heard on the side opposite the leak.

Q-V9.title: Check · USB, cameras and room computers

qs.q: A USB camera drops and reconnects. The conferencing app shows “no camera” until someone reselects it. Why?
o: It came back as a new device instance; the app was set to the old one
qs.why: Select the room camera by type, not one exact instance.

qs.q: At 5 V, a port supplying 0.9 A delivers about…
The camera only vanishes after ten idle minutes while someone presents. First suspect?
o: A power policy suspending idle USB devices
qs.why: Idle, then gone: that's a power state.

qs.q: Roughly how long can a passive USB 2.0 cable run before you need an extender?
qs.why: Beyond that, extend — and test the extender too.

Q-N4.title: Check · Segments and VLANs for AV

qs.q: The camera answers control commands, but the encoder receives no audio stream. Most likely?
o: The encoder's audio card is on a different segment from the stream
qs.why: Control can cross segments; media often can't.

qs.q: Why does AV often get its own VLAN?
o: Media streams, timing and security are different from office traffic

qs.q: A desk move re-patched four ports. Is that a network change?
o: Yes — ports may have changed segment; it needs the network owner and a record

qs.q: Who moves a port to the AV segment?
o: The AV engineer, in the closet
qs.why: The network owner owns the network.

qs.q: Every tile is green; the help desk logged 17 room tickets this morning. First move?
o: Line both up against a third source for the same hours

qs.q: A tile is green but was last heard nine days ago. What should the dashboard do?
o: Show its age and gray out after a threshold
qs.why: Stale isn't healthy or broken; it's unknown.

qs.q: The inventory has 289 rooms; facilities has 300. Coverage is about…
qs.why: 289 ÷ 300 ≈ 96.3% — and the missing 3.7% can never go red.

qs.q: Which is a user-outcome metric?
o: Share of meetings that started clean within two minutes

qs.q: “Green” on Aldermoor's dashboard meant…
o: The room controller answered a ping

qs.q: Why did the eleven exception rooms keep failing on Mondays?
o: They were outside the inventory, so every fleet fix skipped them
qs.why: The ghost lived where nobody could see.

qs.q: What's the honest first entry for the boardroom in the exception register?
o: Owner: unknown — investigate, with a review date
qs.why: Unknown is an answer; blank is a trap.

qs.q: 40 meetings failed; 17 tickets were filed. That's a reporting rate of about…

Q-C3.title: Check · Control systems as state machines

qs.q: A room controller is best described as…
o: A state machine: one state at a time, moved by events

qs.q: What is a guard?
o: A condition that must be true for a transition to happen
qs.why: “Only shut down if nobody is in a call.”

qs.q: Why doesn't a delay fix a race?
o: It only moves the race; when timing changes, the order can flip again
qs.why: Remove the dependency on order: guards and one-at-a-time handling.

qs.q: The panel should show…

Q-A12.title: Check · Speech intelligibility and microphone coverage in meeting rooms

qs.q: Remote listeners struggle with one seat at the end of the table. The likely cause?
o: That seat is outside the microphones' coverage
qs.why: Distance and coverage: the direct speech is weak there.

qs.q: Doubling the talker-to-mic distance changes direct speech by about…
The listening system should be fed with…
o: The loudspeaker output after the volume control
qs.why: Otherwise loop users miss the remote half of every meeting.

qs.q: Best way to verify coverage?
o: One meter reading at the center
A real talker at every seat, heard from the far end
qs.why: Prove it where the listeners are.

qs.q: A display is on the wrong input before a meeting. Switching it back is…
The ninth identical ticket should trigger…
o: A problem record linking all nine

qs.q: A known error record contains…
o: What's known about the cause and the safe workaround

qs.q: Pausing one room's schedule for a day under a pre-approved procedure is a…
What was the underlying cause of the nine incidents?
o: An orphaned 7:00 job on a legacy scheduler nobody owned
qs.why: Human workflow (no owner) → Configuration (an old scheduled job).

qs.q: Where was the first evidence of the cause?
o: In the display's own input-change log
qs.why: The device recorded who switched it.

qs.q: The inventory said “decommissioned.” The lesson?
o: A record can show intent, not reality — verify it
qs.why: Check the world against the record.

qs.q: Why not pull the box's plug the moment you found it?
o: Unknown dependents, not your equipment, and no change
qs.why: Twelve targets. Map first; change second.

Q-S2.title: Check · Least privilege for AV devices

qs.q: Least privilege means…
o: Only the access needed, only for as long as needed

qs.q: Why are shared admin accounts a problem?
o: Nobody can tell who did what

qs.q: A vendor needs an hour on one processor. The best access is…
o: A named, approved, time-limited session to that device only, recorded

qs.q: You find an unrecorded remote agent on a room computer. You…
o: Leave it, record what you saw, report to security

Q-M3.title: Check · Update rings and exception registers

qs.q: Why did a ring of five standard rooms miss the boardroom's failure?
o: None of them had the boardroom's shape — two content inputs

qs.q: An exception register row should include…
o: What differs, why, owner, review date, compensating control, ring membership

qs.q: A vendor update changes a default. Your best protection is…
o: Pin the setting explicitly and test it in a representative ring

qs.q: After a failure in one room, you should…
o: Fix that room and move on
Query the fleet for the same shape
qs.why: Eliminate the failure class, not the instance.

qs.q: Why did the local display show the chart while the far end saw nothing?
o: The display and the far end were fed by different paths; the room computer captured the empty input

qs.q: The fastest safe fixes in the meeting were…
o: The labeled second input, or the laptop-join fallback

qs.q: Why did the update pass testing?
o: Ring 1 had only single-input rooms; the boardroom was an unrecorded exception

qs.q: What eliminated the failure class?
o: Pinning the capture input, representative rings, an exception register and a fleet query
qs.why: One room saved in seconds; four hundred in a week.

Q-V10.title: Check · Sync, genlock and timing references

qs.q: The master reference shows 0 satellites and HOLDOVER. What is it doing?
o: Running on its own oscillator and slowly drifting
qs.why: Holdover buys time; it isn't a fix.

qs.q: A clock is off by 20 ppm. How far does it drift in one hour?
Why did only the older gateway drop out?
o: Its lock range is narrower than the other devices'

qs.q: The backup reference follows the main. Is it a backup?
Video passes through a scaler that adds 5 frames at 29.97 fps; audio isn't delayed. The sound is…
Where should you measure lip sync?
o: At the viewer's end, on the path viewers use
qs.why: Prove it where the people are.

qs.q: Why do planning windows allow more 'late' than 'early'?
o: Our brains expect sound after light

qs.q: An unexplained delay sits on a bus. Best move?
o: Find out why, then label it

qs.q: Sound 5 frames early on the stream only. Where's the cause?
o: The stream path's uncompensated video latency

qs.q: Delay to add when video is 167 ms late and audio already 33 ms?
Why label the delay?
o: So the next careful person knows why it exists

qs.q: Where do you prove the fix?
o: A phone off the station network

qs.q: A promo measures −14 LUFS; the target is −24. What gain brings it to target?
Why can a promo that peaks lower than the news still sound louder?
o: Compression keeps its average loudness high
